bill.title: Improving Veterans’ Experience Act of 2025
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
bill.officialSummary: Improving Veterans’ Experience Act of 2025 This bill establishes the Veterans Experience Office within the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) to carry out the key customer experience initiatives of the VA relating to veterans’ and beneficiaries’ satisfaction with and usage of VA benefits and services. Additionally, the office must require the heads of other organizations and offices within the VA to report regularly on customer experience metrics, action plans, and other customer experience improvement efforts; collect veteran-derived data to determine satisfaction and for use in policymaking; provide strategic guidance and strategies to VA entities for engaging with veterans and beneficiaries; assess and advise the VA on the accuracy and helpfulness of websites and customer-facing information of the VA; and assess and advise the VA on the status and opportunities for improvement of the customer service efforts of the VA. The requirements of this bill terminate on September 30, 2028. The Government Accountability Office must analyze and report on the methodology, effectiveness, and implementation of the VA’s approach to improving veteran and beneficiary customer experience and satisfaction.

classification.plainSummary: This bill creates a new Veterans Experience Office inside the Department of Veterans Affairs to coordinate efforts to improve how satisfied veterans are with VA services. The office would collect feedback from veterans, track customer-service metrics across VA programs, and advise the department on how to make its websites and information more helpful. These requirements would expire in September 2028, and the Government Accountability Office would evaluate how well the approach worked.

industries.rationale: The office's mandate to assess and improve VA websites and digital customer-facing information may affect vendors providing web services and data-collection platforms to the department.

plain.whatItDoes: This bill would set up the Veterans Experience Office within the VA to carry out the key customer experience initiatives of the VA relating to veterans’ and beneficiaries’ satisfaction with and usage of VA benefits and services.
plain.whoItTouches: Veterans and their families. Anyone whose personal data is held by a company.
plain.everydayEffect: If it passed, the change would show up in what the VA does for you. Nothing has changed yet. Most bills never become law.

disclaimer: This tool places two public records next to each other: who donated to a member of Congress, and what that member legislated on. Any overlap you see is a correlation, not causation. It is not evidence of a quid pro quo, of influence, or of wrongdoing. Legislators routinely receive support from industries in their district for the same reason they legislate on them: those industries are there.
